A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CORE context-compression study. All text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v3 Appendices A–D. The relocated prompts and case studies can be matched; v1 ends with references and has no separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA experiments on four datasets, compressor and downstream-model comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analysis and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds detailed Llama compressor comparisons in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 2.2.1 revises warm-start training: v1 discards samples whose summaries do not improve answering; v3 also retains samples answered correctly without a summary but worse with it, assigning an empty target summary. The distillation-plus-GRPO pipeline and reward remain otherwise unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Natural Questions, TriviaQA, HotpotQA and 2WikiMultihopQA with the same Wikipedia retrieval coverage and five-/ten-document scenarios. Appendix D expands model comparisons within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds off-the-shelf Llama3.2-1B/3B and corresponding RECOMP comparisons against CORE, alongside DeepSeek-V3, in the architecture experiments. The comparator membership in the original main and transfer tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported warm-start sample filtering and target assignment change in Section 2.2.1. Appendix D also extends matched-backbone comparisons to RECOMP using Llama 1B/3B configurations. The original evaluation splits, retrievers, document counts and training budgets are retained; rerunning the retained experiments is not established.

E4.justification: Appendix D expands architecture robustness analysis to examine CORE against compression baselines with 1B and 3B backbones, reporting accuracy and token usage. The distillation/GRPO ablations, alpha sensitivity experiment and two case studies are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 Section 3.2 states that each experiment was repeated five times and averages were reported. v3 removes this statement without replacement. This reduces statistical reporting but does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Tables 6–7 add comparator, F1 and token-count results for the existing Llama configurations. Between v1 Figure 5 and v3 Figure 3, CORE-1B TriviaQA EM changes from 64.3 to 64.8 for five documents and 64.8 to 65.2 for ten; ten-document HotpotQA changes from 33.6 to 34.1. Tables 1–3 and the case-study outputs retain their values.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective, advantage normalization and combined reward remain mathematically unchanged. Added cross-entropy, EM and F1 equations spell out existing training and metric operations; there is no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim end-task-driven lossless RAG compression, approximately 3% retained context, a 3.3-point average EM gain, architecture independence and downstream-model transferability. The new conclusion restates these contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning distillation initialization, RL effectiveness, F1 reward sparsity, architecture scaling and answer-critical summaries enabling transfer are retained. Appendix D reiterates the existing robustness interpretation. Neither version provides substantive new limitations of CORE.

D1.justification: v3 retains the prompt templates but omits v1's instructions about randomly sampling three training examples, ordering documents by ascending retrieval score and using identical inputs for downstream-model transfer. Hardware, optimization settings, software frameworks and the promised future code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds citations including DeepSeek-R1, RAG-DDR, Refiner, PISCO, RA-DIT and REPLUG, while the Si et al. prompting citation disappears. The central positioning around end-to-end RL compression remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method and results exposition are extensively rewritten and reorganized. Results gain descriptive subheadings, alpha sensitivity becomes a separate section, and a conclusion and appendix structure are added. These constitute substantial narrative changes beyond the limited scientific additions.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes token-based panels with CORE markers, and Figure 2 is rebuilt into inference and training panels. Architecture and alpha plots are redrawn, with duplicated alpha tick labels appearing in v3 Figure 4. Prompt figures and case tables move to appendices, and Tables 6–7 are added.

improvement.justification: v3 improves organization and pipeline illustration and makes architecture comparisons more detailed. However, it removes five-run averaging and prompt-construction details, while the new tables introduce unexplained DeepSeek discrepancies: top-five TriviaQA EM is 64.13 in Table 1 but 0.6528, equivalent to 65.28%, in Tables 6–7. These presentation gains and reporting regressions prevent a confident judgment of net overall quality improvement.
